name: Agenda or section divider
rule: Use a functional agenda for a long deck; prefer navigation to a decorative cover.

name: Executive decision summary
rule: Show 3-6 stable issue IDs with requested decision, evidence and analysis-page references.

name: Closing decision page
rule: Recover the same issue IDs in a decision table with immediate schedule, owners and judgment criteria; make the close substantive.

name: Repeated item catalog
rule: Repeat the same layout and fields for comparable objects so differences become visible.

name: Time series with KPI lanes
rule: Align management indicators beneath the chart on exactly the same time columns.

name: Bubble priority map
rule: Vertical: share controlled internally; horizontal: years to full benefit; area: annual benefit. Filled means internal control, outline means external prerequisite. Define the upper-left priority zone.

name: Waterfall contribution bridge
rule: Start and end with reconciled totals, or label the final incremental total. Use dashed handoffs and place an action table beside the chart.

name: Proportional funnel
rule: Size stages to counts and annotate the action at the largest loss. A decorative pyramid is not a proportional funnel.

name: Value-chain earnings view
rule: Align process chevrons and quantitative contributions to identical horizontal positions.

name: Distribution cascade
rule: Show receipts, payments and profit on a common scale; emphasize only the organization's retained share.

name: Quantitative logic tree
rule: Put arithmetic operators on branches, concrete actions at leaves, and evaluation columns to the right.

name: Formula decomposition
rule: Use the formula as the vertical structure; begin each compared row with a conclusion about its terms.

name: Same-unit elapsed-time decomposition
rule: Show active work and waiting in proportional bands using the same unit and scale.

name: Common-axis small multiples
rule: Use identical minima, maxima and tick positions for every small chart.

name: Parallel common-process view
rule: Draw the shared process once across the top; stack compared entities vertically beneath matching stages.

name: Common-scale structure comparison
rule: Use one grade, pay or other common scale and place every box at its actual coordinate.

name: Matching flow comparison
rule: Place equivalent flows side by side; label solid goods flows and dashed money flows explicitly.

name: Matching organization comparison
rule: Use the same tree geometry on both sides; encode intervention reach through fill intensity.

name: Risk-profile comparison
rule: Compare coverage on the same two axes, such as impact and likelihood; connect numbered areas to a policy list.

name: Position-preserving before and after
rule: Keep removed items in their original positions using dashed outlines; never pack remaining items into the space.

name: Area recomposition
rule: Show before/after proportional areas with a transformation arrow and dotted prior-state outlines.

name: Paired assumption rewrite
rule: Pair old and new wording; old uses gray/dashed styling and new uses solid primary styling.

name: Composition by efficiency area plot
rule: Width times height represents quantity times quality; draw the correctly weighted overall-average line.

name: Absolute area comparison
rule: Encode real widths and heights for many objects using a shared scale; preserve actual area relationships.

name: Trajectory scatter
rule: Connect annual points in order and annotate the meaning of distinct phases.

name: Cyclic scatter
rule: Connect group points in their actual sequence and use arrows to state direction.

name: Scatter with analytical reference lines
rule: Derive equal-outcome reference lines from their equations; do not draw a guessed separator.

name: Small-multiple scatter with ledger
rule: Use plots for shape and an aligned table for actual values; columns and axes must correspond.

name: Interval-segment scatter
rule: Distinguish start/end markers, and extend continuing intervals beyond the explicit current-time line.

name: Qualified overlap Venn
rule: Disclose approximate/nonproportional areas and emphasize one sourced number, not a falsely exact intersection.

name: Stacked actual and forecast area
rule: Separate actual and forecast within the plot and use dashed forecast boundaries with reconciled totals.

name: Decision matrix and logic
rule: Use two axes that affect the decision, such as duration and nonroutine work; connect the matrix to three explicit decision rules.

name: Lifecycle and corresponding policy
rule: Align policy cells directly beneath lifecycle stages and mark the current state with a vertical line.

name: Cross-complementarity
rule: Use two actors by strengths/weaknesses quadrants, joined diagonally where actual complementary relationships exist.

name: Horizon swimlanes
rule: Use short/medium/long-term benefit lanes against a time axis, show benefit totals on cards and an explicit current-time line.

name: Modular delivery plan
rule: Build on a Gantt skeleton with blocks carrying owners and evidence-backed effects.

name: Phase Gantt
rule: Completed work is filled, planned work is outlined, and a current-time line is explicit.

name: Two-level integrated plan
rule: Align a stream-interaction diagram above the same plan's Gantt using a shared time axis.

name: Decision-forum handoffs
rule: Horizontal axis is review stage, vertical axis is forum; label arrows with transferred documents and source rework duration.

name: Goods and money crossover
rule: Use labeled solid goods and dashed money flows, with sourced amounts and payment terms for each transaction.

name: Layer map
rule: Use layers vertically and families horizontally; quantify the organization's reach with a bracket and defined measure.

name: Value-chain coverage map
rule: Align stages above success factors above player coverage; the uncovered area must support the claim.

name: Organization mapping
rule: Apply numbered category badges to an organization chart and pair them with selection issues beneath it.

name: Overview and focused detail
rule: Put the whole on the left and one enlarged block on the right, joined by dashed callouts with consistent content.

name: Evidence-to-action table
rule: Each cell has a fact followed by its implication/action. Variants: basic, temporal, parallel, and hypothesis testing.

name: Vertical issue tree
rule: Put the governing question at the top, decompose downward and thicken only the most important justified path.

name: Role-based business flow
rule: Lanes are roles, diamonds are decisions, dotted paths are exceptions; label exceptions with sourced rate and added duration.

name: Stakeholder relationship map
rule: Place the focal actor centrally; explicitly distinguish goods as solid, money as dashed and data as dotted relationships.
